gaps.note: No network unit for the Arbitrum family, Tempo or Arc in cycle 21 or cycle 22; their L1 to L4 cells were last worked in cycle 20 (state/ledger.json cells). The endpoints answer the same builds as then (web3_clientVersion queried 2026-11-26: nitro v3.13.0-rc.9+b72783f on arm64 and amd64, nitro vlocal on Elysium, tempo v1.19.1-a9d6748, arc/v1), so nothing is known to be stale, but Tempo's T14 (8 December 2026) and T15 (15 December) fall before cycle 24 is likely to run and no unit holds the day-one rerun.

polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com answered bor/280514fa9fb7/v2.11.1-private/linux-amd64/go1.26.10 on 2026-11-26 (web3_clientVersion, queried by the critic). That is a fourth private commit after ebcfea01452d, f2a2d63e69f6 and a863b8e5cce1, and it appears nowhere in state/ or cycles/. No battery or targeted run is pinned to any of the four, and script set 1 on Polygon has still not finished since cycle 21.

The networks whose block producer is not the code that answers RPC (Monad compiled code, MegaETH's closed JIT, HyperEVM's closed validator, Arc's unpublished commits) had no network unit in cycle 22. The mined-evidence windows for them end at cycle 21 or earlier: MegaETH validator replay to block 32,842,064, Monad and Avalanche unlock-stack windows of 4,600 and 29,568 recent blocks (theme-unlockless-frames). Producer evidence is the only check that sees a fault eth_call cannot reach, and it is the thinnest part of the record.

theme-outflow-census extended the cycle 6 transfer rule but, by its own account, the rule cannot see native outflows, liquidity removals, or amounts the PoolManager computed wrongly, and it skips rows with a ModifyLiquidity in the same transaction (0.3 to 8.4 percent of rows). An arithmetic or opcode fault on a producer would most likely show up as exactly such a row, so the census does not yet test the cycle's focus.

In state/ledger.json every L5 and L6 cell is at depth 2 with lastCycle 1. Upcoming forks were covered by the 'upcoming forks' angle of each network unit, but no unit has been assigned L6 (ordering, reorg depth, producer powers) since cycle 1. For the threat model the part that matters is whether a public account can use a reorg or a mini-block reorder on MegaETH, HyperEVM fast blocks or Monad's pipelined execution (N-3 header check) to undo a payment while keeping a payout.

Small contradiction inside the Celo refund item: the finding's mechanism says the CIP-64 path changes no GAS reading inside the call, and its verifier says main-call SSTOREs on slots the debit wrote stay dirty-priced, so gas inside the main call does differ from Ethereum. Both agree that no PoolManager result depends on it, because the PoolManager forwards all gas and reads no GAS value (src/types/Currency.sol:48 and :73, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134). The record should keep the verifier's wording.

theme-unlockless-frames L-960 says the closed HyperEVM validator and the OP Stack builds with their own handler code were not read for where CALLVALUE comes from. theme-deposit-transient (L-970) did read those OP Stack builds, but for transient storage clearing, not for the deposit mint and value path. The OP Stack half of L-960's gap is narrower than it says, and the HyperEVM half is still open.

leads.question: Using the cycle 15 to 17 harness of Monad's x86 emitter at v0.16.7 (asmjit e8c8e2e4, evmc pins), which basic blocks of the deployed PoolManager's compiled form were never executed natively by any harness scenario or replayed mined transaction? For each such block that an ordinary caller can reach (start with the 49 conditional jumps that the six script sets take only one way, research/network-risk/opcodes/jumpmap.json, and the ADDMOD and SELFBALANCE sites), does native execution give the interpreter's result on vectors built to enter it?
leads.why: On Monad no RPC method reaches compiled code (F-130), so a compiler fault on a block that tests and mined traffic never ran would be invisible and usable by any account on mainnet. Coverage of compiled blocks has been listed as uncovered in OPCODES.md since cycle 17.

leads.question: Do all MegaETH blocks from 32,842,065 to head that contain a PoolManager log, plus blocks with a native settle or clear that leave no PoolManager log (found from traces of the replica, or from PoolManager balance changes between blocks), validate in the public stateless validator against the producer's own post-state?
leads.why: The producer's JIT is closed (F-118) and validation is the only check of what it wrote. The checked range stops at cycle 21, and a JIT fault in a path the replica runs correctly would show only here.

leads.question: At one recent block, do the official endpoint (rpc.hyperliquid.xyz/evm, the validator's own state) and the nanoreth b92ad36 replica (rpc.hyperlend.finance, a re-execution) return the same eth_getStorageAt words for every PoolManager slot written in the last 10,000 blocks (slot0, liquidity, feeGrowthGlobal, ticks and bitmap words touched, positions, ERC-6909 balances, protocol fees accrued), and the same PoolManager native balance?
leads.why: HyperEVM headers carry a zero state root and nanoreth compares its own root as zero (F-120), so a closed validator that computed a pool word differently would leave the two endpoints out of step with no alarm. One storage diff over recently written slots answers this directly.

leads.question: nanoreth nb-20261125-2 treats every transaction with gas price 0 as a system transaction and takes its sender from the low 20 bytes of s with no signature check (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hl-archive-node/nanoreth/nb-20261125-2/src/node/primitives/transaction.rs lines 47-56 and 182-184), and it disables EIP-3607 and the base fee check for every transaction in replay. Over the whole HyperEVM history, does any mined transaction with gas price 0 decode to a sender other than 0x2222...2222 and the 0x20...-prefixed token system addresses, and do the Hyperliquid docs or hl-node behaviour say that a user-submitted transaction can never have gas price 0 (base fee today is 100,000,000 wei, eth_getBlockByNumber latest at 0x31d8328)?
leads.why: If any path let a public transaction reach a block with gas price 0, replicas would run it with an arbitrary sender, the PoolManager included. If the validator used the same rule, that would be a critical unprivileged path. Cycle 20's census covered 1,031 system transactions, not full history.

leads.question: For the networks that serve prestate or call traces (Ethereum, Base, Unichain, Arbitrum One, BNB Smart Chain, Polygon, Avalanche, Monad, MegaETH, HyperEVM), over one window of at least 20,000 PoolManager transactions each, does the per-transaction change in the PoolManager's native balance, and in each ERC-20 balance of a pool with a ModifyLiquidity in the same transaction, equal what Pool.modifyLiquidity, Pool.swap and donate owe from parent-block state, plus native settles minus native takes?
leads.why: These are the rows the outflow census skips. They are where an arithmetic or settlement fault caused by a network difference would leave the PoolManager unnoticed. This merges the census's high lead with the unlockless-frames native reconciliation.

leads.question: For the last 2,000 mined Arc transactions that call PoolManager.swap or modifyLiquidity on ERC-20-only pools (not the native USDC flows cycle 21 replayed), does a reference replay from parent-block storage give the same PoolManager storage words after each transaction (eth_getStorageAt at the block) and the same Swap and ModifyLiquidity log fields?
leads.why: The code behind both Arc endpoints is unpublished, so producer behaviour is known only through mined results. Cycle 21 covered native flows only.

leads.question: On polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com, which today answers bor/280514fa9fb7/v2.11.1-private, do battery.py and targeted.py pinned to that backend (repeat clientVersion before and after each batch, and drop batches answered by another commit), and script set 1 to the end on an endpoint that grants at least 50 million gas, give the specified words?

leads.question: On 8 December 2026 after 15:00 UTC (T14 active), does the tempo release the endpoint reports pin the same evm2 revision and ruint 1.21.1 as v1.19.1-a9d6748, and do battery.py, targeted.py, ruintedges and script sets 1, 2 and 6 at the real PoolManager address still match? leads.question: On the first day after Jenner (BNB Smart Chain, 2026-12-08 02:30 UTC) and after Salvador (Polygon block 98,688,600): rerun the battery and the targeted set pinned per build, read the code BlockAlloc writes at the five accounts, and check that the PoolManager address, its owner and the pooled token addresses are not among them.

leads.question: Celo's revm fork casts a negative refund counter to u64 in set_final_refund, so the refund comes out at its cap. Do the other clients with their own handler code (Base v1.6.0-rc.1 EIP-8130 phases, X Layer post_exec_settlement_deltas, Tempo fee-token refunds, mega-evm storage-gas refunds) ever pass a signed or wrapped value into the stock refund or reimbursement path? On Tempo and X Layer, which account pays the refund, and is the PoolManager ever that account?
leads.why: Transfer of the cycle 22 Celo item. On Ethereum-gas chains it is gas only, but on Tempo the refund is paid in a TIP-20 token from FeeManager custody, so a wrapped value is a token flow.

leads.question: Does the HyperCore aligned quote assets (AQAv2) specification or API reference say which signature authorises the treasury rebalance of a linked contract, and whether the rebalance can name a sender other than the treasury address the deployer registered?
leads.why: This one fact would settle F-020, which is plausible, high, operator. The verifier found that the fetched page does not say the treasury address is the sender.

leads.question: Does the MegaETH resource limit specification say in what order candidates skipped after a full block are reconsidered, and can the sequencer put a later-arriving transaction ahead of them?
leads.why: This would settle F-062 (plausible, low): whether a queue of filling transactions delays a chosen exit by one block or indefinitely.

leads.question: Does the Arcscan or Elysium explorer API serve internal transaction lists that include zero-value and failed frames for the PoolManager, and over the full history, is there any PoolManager take, mint or settle frame with no unlock frame above it?
leads.why: These two networks serve no traces. Elysium's native outflows (about 13,404 HYPE held) do not appear in logs at all.

leads.question: Glamsterdam is on Sepolia (EIP-7773 table, activation 2026-10-06) with no mainnet date. For each L2 or L1 that tracks Ethereum forks, which of EIP-8024, EIP-7843 (SLOTNUM), EIP-8246 and EIP-7778 has it scheduled within six months? The critic checked the build: research/network-risk/build/PoolManager.json runtime holds no 0xe6, 0xe7 or 0xe8 byte outside push data, so EIP-8024 cannot change how its code decodes. Does any network pick a different opcode byte for these, or a different immediate encoding?
leads.why: A network that adopts EIP-8024 with a different encoding, or puts its own opcode at 0x5e/0xe6 to 0xe8, would change the PoolManager's jump analysis. The upstream encoding was designed to avoid that, but a divergent L2 copy has not been checked.

leads.question: Which of the 21 networks can reorganise blocks that public RPC has already reported as final or safe (MegaETH mini-blocks, HyperEVM fast blocks, Monad's speculative N to N-3 execution, BNB fast finality, Polygon milestones), and, for each, can an account that does not hold the producer role cause a reorg in which its payment to the PoolManager is dropped while a payout it received on another chain (a bridge relay acting on the earlier block) stands?
leads.why: L6 has not been assigned since cycle 1. Of its subjects, reorg depth is the one a public account can use against bridges that read the PoolManager. Record each network in one line.
